method: EventTarget fixture executes current BrowserInput TypeScript; validates axis/aim/edge ownership and device isolation, without changing or mocking game rules.

checks.name: touch mode starts stationary with upward default aim
partial joystick deflection keeps analog movement magnitude
diagonal deflection clamps to unit speed without distorting direction
out of range finite axes preserve ratio and clamp magnitude
enormous finite axes cannot overflow normalization
invalid axes immediately stop and preserve the last valid facing
recentring stops at the next tick without rotating a held aim
last nonzero direction survives recentering for the next selection
real joystick axis changes update an existing preview
Boss motion and repeated axes do not rebase mobile aiming
every screen pointer type is ignored while touch mode is active
right finger motion cannot move the Boss when the left stick is centred
touch release is copied before later axis or screen pointer changes
holding and releasing mobile skill remains one edge without auto fire
mobile latest owner wins and old pointer release is ignored
old pointer cancellation preserves a replaced mobile owner
matching pointer cancellation cancels its mobile release packet
mobile cancel preserves movement while discarding held or pending skills
Space cancels mobile aim and retains analog movement
keyboard movement temporarily overrides joystick and releases back to analog
currently held keyboard direction supplies new aim before joystick fallback
keyboard remains a remembered facing fallback when no joystick direction exists
keyboard movement does not rotate an existing touch aim by itself
switching into touch mode clears held keys, mouse and released skill edges
repeated touch mode assignment does not interrupt a gesture
switching back to mouse cancels mobile state and requires a fresh mouse event
clear resets joystick and facing while preserving mobile mode
window blur clears mobile movement, preview and delayed release
restart clears joystick and pending releases before callback
pause clears mobile input before invoking the existing pause callback
nonplaying phase prevents mobile selection and later release
desktop ignores touch and pen contacts without losing the real mouse target
desktop accepts empty synthetic pointerType and ignores inactive joystick updates
getSelection stays defensive for mobile previews
dispose detaches pointer and keyboard listeners and clears axes
